- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap forecast decline to 5–10% below peak to avoid overshoot.
- If 3+ consecutive forecast values are above 80, model tends to overestimate; apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 2–3 periods.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model misreads momentum; adjust forecast to align with sentiment trend direction, not absolute magnitude.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term mean reversion; reduce forecast by 1–2% for each period after 10–15 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
